Make a game-wide Mac bootstrap

All 17 BSPs have typed local exports; six BSP-used victim ACTs plus herodown decode locally; referenced actor cues resolve to the recovered sound bank. Static lookup maps unknown boy1 to boy/model 11/vic_boy.act; model 14 selects renderer IDs 11-13 and their ACT paths while retaining its victim resource definition; victim materials cycle per selected model ID and update slot 0. The shared viewer keeps world model 0 enabled for BoundsTriggers without model references. The viewer submits trigger-associated mesh groups through its ordinary render path; trigger-model collision exclusion is separate. The rescue scene preview also bundles a provisional ACT asset-inspection loader; its inherited decoder is near-identical to the legacy map explorer and needs independent retail validation. All seven rescue maps have grounded collision/texture baselines. Interactive victim placement, lightmaps/material parity, and original menu flow remain open. The original Direct3D callback boundary and the distinct RRF sprite/effect/HUD asset path are documented.

Next: Confirm actor presentation in the interactive macOS bundle; continue the level-neutral SceneData/catalog resolver and actor-to-surface binding trace.
M5in progress

Reach a rescue campaign slice on Mac

The map-neutral preview loads typed victims, applies the traced spawn/roam rules, constructs authored FireEntity instances before victim startup, and draws their retail sprite frames. The recovered FireUpdate state/alpha transition runs in the rendered loop with no-op light/bookkeeping and state-4 path-motion callbacks; random proximity spread is wired through the mapped FireRescue contact callback with the 750-unit gate, child shape/timing, collision sweep, and deferred creation, Current-hash PlayerRescue root slot +0x0C maps to thunk 0049DB90 and the viewer uses Player::p as a provisional origin adapter; getter body and alignment remain open. The FireRescue root +0x48 string-length gate maps to nonempty A_Name; unnamed authored fires and generated children do not spread. Callback cadence remains provisional. Selected extinguisher use now applies source-derived sampled contacts and nonterminal suppression through message 30000. The viewer camera parent frame and rendered-frame cadence remain provisional; player exposure and terminal visual lifecycle remain open; extinguisher particles now consume the source-shaped request with a provisional resource-14 texture pair, two-second lifetime, cooldown, and velocity, while natural hit feedback and exact particle presentation remain unverified. The shared goggles scan now filters kinds 2 and 6 within the retail 2,000-unit range and excludes victim states 5/6; resource 703 heatpulse markers draw at approximate host target positions for the verified 8.5-second effect window. Retail actor-local transform and child attachment are not reproduced; marker size, placement, blend/tint, child animation, and global visibility remain provisional or open. The 38 copied flame/glow BMPs have per-file hashes. Earlier MiscEmitter draws, UserData radius binding, and exact engine turn/move remain open. Shared pickup is wired. The authored MBase tell player escape binding reaches VictimTransactions::escape; synthetic headless checks pass on Training and all seven campaign rescue BSPs. Carried-body presentation, live exit scheduling, axe behavior, goggles child animation/visibility semantics, final equipment state, and mission completion remain open. Bank `--interaction-check` triggers entity 541 and reaches PATH time 1 without M, then deliberately waits for the endpoint, centers with a short side-step, and crosses using Player::step plus the live child collision pose. This controlled pass does not establish ordinary approach timing. Source confirms M/N only affect PATH inspection state; the user-reported M workaround still needs an ordinary live-route reproduction. Bank should start open, but the user reports an opaque obstruction at startup. A fresh offscreen render check submitted all 497/497 mesh groups and decoded/uploaded 105/105 textures; a dark polygon remains unmatched to the user's view. Face alpha/flags and lightmaps are not preserved through export, so original material behavior is unresolved. The latest app-bundled executable was reported hash-matched to its build output. Gas R and Bank render checks draw 39/72 FireRescue actors (156/288 sprite quads). Authored Player climb/unclimb commands now toggle the existing climbing state, but the Training ladder check could not find a clear contact position; end-to-end ladder behavior is unverified.

Next: Reproduce the ordinary Bank door approach and diagnose contact/PATH/render/collision without M. Match the fresh obstruction to the user's start view and preserve face material data. Trace fog and red surfaces, then validate authored ladder contact and climbing. Refresh the PlayerRescue getter body and fourth-float initialization, validate FireRescue callback cadence and child lifecycle, then integrate player exposure; complete axe use, dynamic goggles child animation/visibility semantics, and rescue flow, then extend to every campaign rescue.
